title: THE LAST AUDIENCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF NINE HARBOURS
deck: A dying governor has asked to see the daughter he exiled, and four hundred families are waiting outside with thirty years of stamped replies. Illuminara can shelter a room, but she cannot make a tyrant honest or forgive on anyone's behalf, so she reads the wall until she finds the one question nobody ever asked him in his own language.
shape: Seven scenes across four days and a morning: a wall of stamped answers, a daughter's terms, a night of sorting paper, a reasonable man's counteroffer, a book read aloud page by page, a door that only one person may open, and a quarry at dawn.

scenes.title: The Wall
paragraphs: *Arrivals concourse, Vesper Rest hospice · first of four days, 14:05*

Four hundred and twelve families had come to the hospice before the governor's shuttle was cold, and none of them had said a word aloud. They had come from all nine harbours, and until that week most of them had never met. They stood along the concourse wall in the order they had arrived, each holding the one paper they had carried for thirty years: a petition in their own handwriting on the top half, and below it a purple stamp.

Illuminara read the nearest before she reached the woman waiting for her. *RELOCATED. NO FURTHER ENQUIRY.* A number sat under the stamp in small type. The next paper said the same. So did the one after.
The woman at the head of the wall was past sixty, with a pilot's squint and a scarf wound twice. She did not offer a hand.

**Davi Orsolo**  
You will shelter his last words, and our dead will wait outside as usual.

**Illuminara**  
I can shelter a room. I cannot make him honest, I cannot forgive for anyone standing here, and I cannot make one of you come in. If nobody comes, it is only a room.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Then tell me what you are for.

**Illuminara**  
I don't know yet. Tell me what you would take instead of a room.
Davi looked at her for a while. Behind her, four hundred people had gone so still that the air handlers were the loudest thing in the concourse.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Not his sorrow. Three governors' spokesmen have offered us his sorrow. A man who signs that many papers keeps something. Whatever he kept, we want it, and we want it before he is dead and his successors have time to be tidy.

**Illuminara**  
I can't promise you he kept anything. I can promise I won't tell you it's enough that he was visited.
It was not much, and Davi seemed to know it was not much, and she nodded once anyway, the way a pilot acknowledges an honest depth.

Illuminara did not leave. She went on down the wall, one paper at a time. *Purple, purple, purple,* she thought, and under each the small number, and no family on this floor had ever stood beside another family's paper.

scenes.title: The Daughter's Terms
paragraphs: *Guest room three, Vesper Rest · first day, 22:30*

Ilen Marrow had taken her mother's name the day her father exiled her, and she had kept it for twenty-two years. She was fifty-three, a harbour teacher by trade, and she poured the tea herself and did not ask whether Illuminara took sugar.

**Ilen**  
He is good at rooms. I want you to understand that before you shelter one. The order that sent me off the Harbours was read to me in the kindest voice I have ever heard. He asked whether I had eaten.

**Illuminara**  
What had you done?

**Ilen**  
Refused to read a statement. A teacher at my school had taught the children something he shouldn't, and I was to say I had seen it. I hadn't. My father called exile a protection. Maybe he even believed it. That is the thing about him. He can believe it while he does it.
She set the pot down with great care.

**Ilen**  
He will make this room so good that I will thank him for the chair. So these are my terms. I will not sit across from him while those people stand in that concourse. I won't be what he buys, and I won't be what they bargain with. Do whatever you have to do for them first. Then ask me. I may still say no.

**Illuminara**  
You may.

**Ilen**  
Is he capable of being anything else?
Illuminara had been waiting for the question since the shuttle, and found she had no clean answer to give it.

**Illuminara**  
I don't know. And I won't read it off him and carry it back to you. If I told you yes, you would be taking my word for your father, and you have had enough of people telling you what he is.
Ilen laughed, short and surprised, and it cost her something.

In the pause Illuminara thought of her own mother's kitchen, and of a voice asking whether she had eaten, and set the thought aside carefully, so that it would not become an argument for either of them.

**Ilen**  
Then what will you do?

**Illuminara**  
Go and read the wall. Whatever he did to those people, he did it in a form. I'd like to see which one.

scenes.title: What the Stamp Says
paragraphs: *Arrivals concourse · second day, 03:10*

By three in the morning most of the families were asleep sitting up, their papers on their knees. Davi was not. She had brought Illuminara a cup of something hot without comment and gone back to her place, and Illuminara had spent two hours going down the wall one stamp at a time.
She stopped at a paper near the middle, went back four, and then forward six.

**Illuminara**  
Who holds one-eighteen?

A man two places along raised his hand without waking fully. One-seventeen was beside him. One-nineteen was across the concourse. They were not in the order of the wall. They were in the order of something else.

**Illuminara**  
Davi. Help me put these on the floor.

It took the better part of an hour, thirty families waking one by one and passing a paper along without asking why. When the floor was covered, the numbers ran from one to four hundred and twelve with no gap. Each family had carried a single stamp for thirty years. This was the first time the stamps had lain side by side.

**Illuminara**  
It isn't a refusal. It's a citation. He numbered them in the order he did them, and he filed them somewhere a number could find. Nobody knew the numbers ran in a line, because nobody had ever seen two.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Mine asked where.
She held it out. *Where is Pell Orsolo, harbour pilot?* in her hand at thirty-three, and under it the same purple, and a number.

**Illuminara**  
Then I'm only half right. He could stamp a question he was asked in your words. Did you quote him his own number?

**Davi Orsolo**  
I didn't have it.

**Illuminara**  
Nobody did. A page he had to look up would have been the one thing he could not stamp. I don't say it would have made him honest. I say it could not have been answered from the drawer.

**Davi Orsolo**  
He has lied since before I was married.

**Illuminara**  
Then what stops him handing you a book full of false graves?
Davi had been a pilot's wife and was now a pilot's widow in everything but paper. She answered the way her husband would have.

**Davi Orsolo**  
A pilot doesn't trust the harbour master's chart. He asks the pilots who have been in. Every family writes one thing on a card that only they know. His boot size. What he said at the door. A man can invent a grave. He cannot invent my husband's whistle.

**Illuminara**  
And nothing he gives is traded. No audience, no pardon, no promise from anyone. If he gives you the book, he gives it for nothing, because it was never his to sell.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Say that again.

**Illuminara**  
It was never his to sell.

**Davi Orsolo**  
He won't do it.

**Illuminara**  
Then you will have asked him a question in his own language and he will have refused it, and the room stays empty. I'm not going to pretend that can't happen.

**Davi Orsolo**  
And if he does? My husband's name, read out in his voice?

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Davi Orsolo**  
I'll want it read twice.

She called a clerk's name down the concourse before Illuminara could answer. Hesper Duell had kept the registry at Fourth Harbour for forty years and had a brother on the wall. The cards would go in sealed envelopes to her, and she would read him each number and set his answer against the card. If it was not on the card, they stopped. Nobody would be asked to attend, and nobody would be asked to forgive. Davi said it twice, to the sleepers and the waking, and wrote it on the back of a petition.

scenes.title: A Reasonable Man
paragraphs: *Governor Thesk's room · second day, 19:00*

Ruvane Thesk was small under the blanket, and his hands were very clean. He had governed Nine Harbours for thirty years and had learned in the first of them that the quickest way to disarm a visitor was to be glad to see her.

**Thesk**  
You are punctual. I'd heard. Please sit. I can't offer you tea. They have me on something worse.
Illuminara sat. She told him the terms in four sentences and then stopped, because four sentences were all she had.
He took his time. When he spoke it was in the easy tone of a man who has chaired a great many meetings and wishes to be helpful.

**Thesk**  
Then let me improve it. The book goes to my daughter. She is its heir. She can decide whom it serves. A gift from a father to a daughter, and nobody needs to stand in a concourse.

**Illuminara**  
No.

**Thesk**  
You haven't heard my reasons.

**Illuminara**  
I've heard one. It makes her the thing you give. Tell me the rest.

**Thesk**  
There are officers in that book who sit in the harbour offices today. Some are decent now. Some have children who were born afterwards. The examiner at Seventh Harbour signs every pilot's licence on the Harbours, and he is on page forty. Read his name to a full room before a court has asked him anything and no pilot will take a licence from him by Friday, and nobody will fly. You are proposing to put a lit match into a country that has been quiet for thirty years. And you will be applauded for it.
That was his best argument, and he knew it, and Illuminara did not pretend it was a weak one.

**Illuminara**  
I didn't know about the examiner. I can't take his name out of the book, and neither can you. Is there a way to read it so that Seventh Harbour still has an examiner on Friday?

**Thesk**  
I don't know. I have been asking myself since the shuttle.

**Illuminara**  
Then I'll carry it to them as something you said. Not as a condition. They may refuse it.

He closed his eyes, and for a moment looked his age. When he opened them he drew the book across the blanket toward her, the black cloth gone grey at the corners, and turned it open to show her the pages. His thumb passed over forty-one of them without touching, the way a man steps over a stair he knows is broken.

**Thesk**  
The last forty-one entries are not in my hand. My deputy, Corvin Hale, kept them in his own shorthand, and he has been dead nine years. I can read the numbers and the names. I cannot read where. A book with forty-one pages I can't read is not a book I can give properly. I have not slept well about it.

Illuminara watched the thumb go over them again, and understood what had been underneath the kindness. It was not fear of the match, nor of the officers, nor even of his daughter. It was a clerk's fear, of an unfinished page.

**Illuminara**  
The form asks each family for a fact only they know, and sets it against your page. Where your page is empty, theirs may not be.

**Thesk**  
They would help me finish it.

**Illuminara**  
They would help themselves. They would not be helping you.

**Thesk**  
Yes. That is the correct way to put it.
He was silent for a long time.

**Thesk**  
And Ilen?

**Illuminara**  
Nothing is promised. She will decide afterwards, and she may say no.

**Thesk**  
Then I am to give away the only thing I have, and for nothing.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Thesk**  
I have never done that.

**Illuminara**  
I believe you.

His hand went to the glass on the tray and shook so badly the water slopped. Illuminara got there first and held it to him. She did not know whether it was kindness or complicity to hold a glass for this man, and held it anyway, because it was what was in front of her, and made no claim for it, to him or to herself.

**Thesk**  
Why are you here? For her? For them?

**Illuminara**  
For whoever is in front of me. Tonight that is you. I won't tell you it's all right.

**Thesk**  
Good. I would have stopped believing you.
He set the glass down himself.

**Thesk**  
Bring your clerk at six.

scenes.title: Page by Page
paragraphs: *Registry room, Vesper Rest · third day, 06:00*

The registry room was the only space on the asteroid with a table large enough, and Hesper Duell had arranged it as she had arranged forty years of rooms: the governor's chair at one end, a desk of sealed envelopes at the other, and nothing between them but the book. It was larger than Illuminara had pictured and plainer, bound in black cloth gone grey at the corners. A second, smaller room stood open off it, with two chairs.
Illuminara had carried the examiner to Davi in the small hours. She had expected a refusal and had been told to wait for the morning.

**Davi Orsolo**  
I won't have one name held back for his sake. Not one.

**Hesper Duell**  
Nothing is held back. Each page is read first in the small room, to the family it belongs to, in full. The hall hears it if they say so. Any page naming an officer still in office is copied in my hand to the courts' registrar the same hour. A court can sit him down. A roomful of us can't.

**Davi Orsolo**  
And Friday? Seventh has no examiner.

**Hesper Duell**  
Seventh has no examiner until the court is done. That is a cost, and it falls on pilots who did nothing.
Davi looked at the open door of the small room for a moment, and then at the book.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Then read.
Thirty families had written cards. Hesper broke the first envelope with a paper knife.

**Hesper Duell**  
Page ninety-four. What did she say at the door?

**Thesk**  
The entry says, 'Is the kettle on.' It is a small hand. A note beneath: 'She laughed.'
Hesper looked at the card in her hand and then at the governor, and said nothing. The woman who had written it stood in the doorway, and Illuminara watched her hand go to her mouth.
Twenty-nine of the thirty matched. The thirtieth was a card from a family whose page was in Hale's shorthand.

**Thesk**  
I can't read that one. I could invent something you would like. I would rather you knew which is which.

**Hesper Duell**  
A forger fills the gap. He left it. Continue.

That was how the book began. He read in stretches of forty minutes, and then his voice went and they waited, and nobody told him to hurry. Each page went first to its family in the small room, and most families then asked for it again in the hall, and a few did not. Illuminara sat by the door with her hands on her knees and did what the window did, and no more: it kept the room from becoming anyone's stage. It could not make the names lighter.
At page two hundred and twelve he stopped and could not go on.

**Thesk**  
I can't do this one.
Illuminara said nothing. Neither did Hesper. The room waited. After a while he drew the page toward him and began.
Pell Orsolo's page came a little after two the next morning. Davi had asked for the hall. She had been standing at the back since midnight.

**Thesk**  
Orsolo, Pell. Harbour pilot, Ninth Harbour. Ballast-ice quarry, section C, forty metres under the loading rail. Stamped relocated, by order of the Governor.
Davi did not move.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Again.

**Thesk**  
Orsolo, Pell. Harbour pilot. Section C, under the loading rail. By my order.
Davi nodded, as one nods to a reading that agrees with the chart, and went out. Illuminara did not follow her.

By dawn of the fourth day three hundred and seventy-one pages had been read, and a woman near the back remembered that Hale's men had called the quarry barge *the Sparrow*, and that closed one of the forty-one. A man remembered a date. By noon nineteen of Hale's pages had been closed by the people they belonged to. Twenty-two stayed open, and nobody in the room pretended they would not.

When the last page had been read, Hesper took the book into the registry's custody and sealed it with her cord. Thesk had asked to keep it by his bed, and she lent it to him on those terms, sealed, with a receipt that said so. No page could be cut from it now. Pages could only be read.

scenes.title: The Door
paragraphs: *Corridor outside the governor's room · fourth day, 21:40*

Hesper's verdict had gone down the concourse on the morning the reading began: thirty cards, twenty-nine matches, one honest gap. Crews with spades had already left on the evening tender for the quarry at Ninth Harbour, and the books of the dead had begun, at last, to be the books of the found.
Ilen stood in the corridor with her hands pulled into her sleeves. Illuminara waited a pace away, because she had been asked to wait there.

**Ilen**  
I said the book first. It has been first. Now I have to find out whether I want to.

**Illuminara**  
You can still say no. Nothing here is owed.

**Ilen**  
I know. That is the only reason I can go in.

The door opened for a nurse, and Illuminara saw into the room before it shut. He had not arranged it. The blanket was crooked, the good chair stood against the wall where the nurse had left it, and there was no tea on the tray. He had not sat up to receive anyone.

Ilen went in alone. Illuminara kept the window closed behind her and did nothing else. Twenty-six minutes. Through the door came two voices, one steady and one ragged, and the ragged one was not always his.
When Ilen came out she looked older and lighter at once.

**Ilen**  
He asked whether I had eaten.

**Illuminara**  
What did you say?

**Ilen**  
That it was a very good question and I wasn't going to answer it. Then I told him all of it. He didn't manage me. He listened. I am not going to tell you what he said.

**Illuminara**  
You don't have to.

Ruvane Thesk died at ten past four in the morning with the sealed book shut on the table beside his bed, on Hesper's loan, and her clerk's receipt for it in his hand. Illuminara was in the room. He had asked for someone, and the nurse had run out of volunteers. She did not take his hand and she did not leave. When it was over she told the nurse the time.

scenes.title: Section C
paragraphs: *Ballast-ice quarry, Ninth Harbour · fifth day, 06:30*

The loading rail was frosted white, and forty metres below it the first crew had cut through the lid of the section. Davi stood at the rim in her twice-wound scarf with a page in her coat, a fair copy in Hesper's neat hand that said, in the governor's words, where her husband was.

**Davi Orsolo**  
I have not forgiven him.

**Illuminara**  
Nobody asked you to.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Good. Don't.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Seventh Harbour has no examiner this morning. Half the pilots on the Harbours are grounded till the court sits, and some of them are saying it was us.

**Illuminara**  
It was. Do you want me to say otherwise?

**Davi Orsolo**  
No.

Down in the cut a spade rang on ice, and then on something that was not ice. Along the rim, people who had stood silent in a concourse for four days began, one by one, to speak. Davi took out the page and read it aloud to her son, who had been seven when the pilot boat did not come back. She read it twice, because she had been told it was allowed.

critic_line: Illuminara discovers that the purple stamps are serialized citations rather than answers, accepts Davi's counterexample and narrows her claim, then carries Thesk's strongest objection back to the families without turning it into his condition; the families, their clerk, Ilen and even Thesk retain their own choices, while an authenticated book returns 390 locations, leaves 22 honestly open, sends serving officers toward court and leads Davi to Pell Orsolo's quarry without requiring forgiveness.

translation_sl.title: ZADNJA AVDIENCA GUVERNERJA DEVETIH PRISTANIŠČ
translation_sl.deck: Umirajoči guverner je prosil, da bi videl hčer, ki jo je izgnal, zunaj pa s tridesetimi leti žigosanih odgovorov čaka štiristo družin. Illuminara lahko zavaruje sobo, ne more pa tirana prisiliti k iskrenosti ali odpustiti v imenu kogarkoli, zato bere zid, dokler ne najde vprašanja, ki mu ga v njegovem lastnem jeziku ni zastavil še nihče.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v štirih dneh in enem jutru: zid žigosanih odgovorov, hčerini pogoji, noč razvrščanja papirjev, nasprotni predlog razumnega človeka, knjiga, prebrana stran za stranjo, vrata, ki jih lahko odpre le ena oseba, ter kamnolom ob zori.

scenes.title: Zid
paragraphs: *Prihodni hodnik, hospic Vesper Rest · prvi od štirih dni, 14:05*

Štiristo dvanajst družin je prišlo v hospic, še preden se je guvernerjev raketoplan ohladil, in nobena ni na glas izrekla niti besede. Prišle so iz vseh devetih pristanišč in do tistega tedna se večina med seboj ni nikoli srečala. Ob zidu hodnika so stale po vrstnem redu prihoda, vsaka z edinim listom, ki ga je nosila trideset let: na zgornji polovici prošnja v lastni pisavi, pod njo pa vijoličen žig.

Illuminara je prebrala najbližji list, še preden je prišla do ženske, ki jo je čakala. *PREMEŠČEN. BREZ NADALJNJIH POIZVEDB.* Pod žigom je bila z drobnim tiskom zapisana številka. Na naslednjem listu je pisalo enako. Tudi na tistem za njim.
Ženska na čelu vrste ob zidu je imela več kot šestdeset let, pilotov zoženi pogled in dvakrat ovit šal. Roke ji ni ponudila.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Ti boš zavarovala njegove zadnje besede, naši mrtvi pa bodo kakor običajno čakali zunaj.

**Illuminara**  
Lahko zavarujem sobo. Ne morem ga prisiliti k iskrenosti, ne morem odpustiti v imenu nikogar, ki stoji tukaj, in nikogar od vas ne morem prisiliti, da vstopi. Če ne pride nihče, je to samo soba.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Potem mi povej, čemu služiš.

**Illuminara**  
Tega še ne vem. Povej mi, kaj bi sprejela namesto sobe.
Davi jo je nekaj časa gledala. Za njo je štiristo ljudi tako obmirovalo, da so bile prezračevalne naprave najglasnejša stvar v hodniku.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Ne njegovega obžalovanja. Tiskovni predstavniki treh guvernerjev so nam že ponujali njegovo obžalovanje. Človek, ki podpiše toliko listov, nekaj obdrži. Karkoli je obdržal, hočemo to, in hočemo, preden umre in imajo njegovi nasledniki čas, da vse pospravijo.

**Illuminara**  
Ne morem vam obljubiti, da je karkoli obdržal. Lahko pa obljubim, da vam ne bom rekla, da zadostuje že to, da ga je nekdo obiskal.
Ni bilo veliko in zdelo se je, da Davi ve, da ni veliko, pa je vseeno enkrat pokimala, kakor pilot potrdi pošteno izmerjeno globino.

Illuminara ni odšla. Nadaljevala je vzdolž zidu, po en list naenkrat. *Vijolično, vijolično, vijolično,* je pomislila, in pod vsakim majhna številka; nobena družina v tem nadstropju še nikoli ni stala ob listu druge družine.

scenes.title: Hčerini pogoji
paragraphs: *Soba za goste tri, Vesper Rest · prvi dan, 22:30*

Ilen Marrow je na dan, ko jo je oče izgnal, prevzela materin priimek in ga obdržala dvaindvajset let. Imela je triinpetdeset let, po poklicu je bila pristaniška učiteljica, čaj pa je nalila sama in Illuminare ni vprašala, ali ga pije s sladkorjem.

**Ilen**  
Dober je v sobah. Hočem, da to razumeš, preden eno zavaruješ. Ukaz, s katerim so me poslali iz Pristanišč, so mi prebrali z najprijaznejšim glasom, kar sem jih kdaj slišala. Vprašal me je, ali sem jedla.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj si storila?

**Ilen**  
Nisem hotela prebrati izjave. Učitelj na moji šoli je otroke učil nečesa, česar ne bi smel, jaz pa naj bi rekla, da sem to videla. Nisem. Moj oče je izgon imenoval zaščita. Morda je v to celo verjel. Prav to je pri njem. Lahko verjame, medtem ko to počne.
Čajnik je odložila z veliko previdnostjo.

**Ilen**  
To sobo bo naredil tako prijetno, da se mu bom zahvalila za stol. Zato so moji pogoji taki. Ne bom sedela nasproti njega, medtem ko ti ljudje stojijo v hodniku. Ne bom tisto, kar bo kupil, in ne bom tisto, s čimer bodo trgovali oni. Najprej naredi zanje, karkoli moraš. Potem me vprašaj. Še vedno lahko rečem ne.

**Illuminara**  
Lahko.

**Ilen**  
Je sploh sposoben biti kaj drugega?
Illuminara je to vprašanje pričakovala že od raketoplana in ugotovila, da zanj nima čistega odgovora.

**Illuminara**  
Ne vem. In tega ne bom razbrala iz njega ter prinesla nazaj tebi. Če bi rekla da, bi za besedo o svojem očetu morala verjeti meni, ljudje pa so ti že dovoljkrat govorili, kakšen je.
Ilen se je kratko in presenečeno zasmejala, in to jo je nekaj stalo.
V premoru je Illuminara pomislila na kuhinjo svoje matere in na glas, ki jo sprašuje, ali je jedla, nato pa je misel previdno odložila, da ne bi postala argument za katerokoli od njiju.

**Ilen**  
Kaj boš potem storila?

**Illuminara**  
Šla bom brat zid. Karkoli je storil tem ljudem, je storil v obrazcu. Rada bi videla, v katerem.

scenes.title: Kaj pravi žig
paragraphs: *Prihodni hodnik · drugi dan, 03:10*

Do treh zjutraj je večina družin zaspala sede, z listi na kolenih. Davi ni. Illuminari je brez besed prinesla skodelico nečesa vročega in se vrnila na svoje mesto, Illuminara pa je dve uri hodila vzdolž zidu, od žiga do žiga.
Ustavila se je pri listu blizu sredine, se vrnila za štiri in nato šla naprej za šest.

**Illuminara**  
Kdo ima sto osemnajst?

Moški dve mesti stran je dvignil roko, ne da bi se povsem prebudil. Sto sedemnajst je bil ob njem. Sto devetnajst na drugi strani hodnika. Niso bili v vrstnem redu zidu. Bili so v vrstnem redu nečesa drugega.

**Illuminara**  
Davi. Pomagaj mi jih položiti na tla.

Trajalo je skoraj uro; trideset družin se je prebujalo druga za drugo in si brez vprašanj podajalo liste. Ko so bila tla prekrita, so številke brez ene same vrzeli tekle od ena do štiristo dvanajst. Vsaka družina je trideset let nosila en sam žig. Prvič so žigi ležali drug ob drugem.

**Illuminara**  
To ni zavrnitev. To je sklic. Oštevilčil jih je po vrstnem redu svojih dejanj in jih nekje shranil tako, da jih je mogoče najti po številki. Nihče ni vedel, da številke tvorijo zaporedje, ker nihče še nikoli ni videl dveh.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Na mojem je pisalo, kje.
Ponudila ji ga je. *Kje je Pell Orsolo, pristaniški pilot?* v njeni pisavi pri triintridesetih, spodaj isto vijolično in številka.

**Illuminara**  
Potem imam prav samo napol. Vprašanje, ki ste mu ga zastavili s svojimi besedami, je lahko žigosal. Si mu navedla njegovo številko?

**Davi Orsolo**  
Nisem je imela.

**Illuminara**  
Nihče je ni imel. Stran, ki bi jo moral poiskati, bi bila edina stvar, ki je ne bi mogel odgovoriti iz predala. Ne pravim, da bi ga prisilila k iskrenosti. Pravim, da nanjo ne bi mogel odgovoriti iz predala.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Laže že od časa, preden sem se poročila.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj mu potem preprečuje, da vam izroči knjigo, polno izmišljenih grobov?
Davi je bila pilotova žena in zdaj v vsem razen na papirju pilotova vdova. Odgovorila je tako, kakor bi njen mož.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Pilot ne zaupa karti pristaniškega poveljnika. Vpraša pilote, ki so že pripluli. Vsaka družina na kartico zapiše eno stvar, ki jo pozna samo ona. Njegovo številko čevljev. Kaj je rekel pri vratih. Človek si lahko izmisli grob. Ne more si izmisliti žvižga mojega moža.

**Illuminara**  
In nič od tega, kar izroči, ni predmet trgovine. Nobene avdience, nobene pomilostitve, nobene obljube od kogarkoli. Če vam da knjigo, jo da za nič, ker je nikoli ni imel pravice prodajati.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Povej še enkrat.

**Illuminara**  
Nikoli je ni imel pravice prodajati.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Tega ne bo storil.

**Illuminara**  
Potem mu boste zastavili vprašanje v njegovem lastnem jeziku in ga bo zavrnil, soba pa bo ostala prazna. Ne bom se pretvarjala, da se to ne more zgoditi.

**Davi Orsolo**  
In če bo? Ime mojega moža, prebrano z njegovim glasom?

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Hotela ga bom slišati dvakrat.

Še preden je Illuminara utegnila odgovoriti, je Davi po hodniku poklicala ime uradnice. Hesper Duell je štirideset let vodila register v Četrtem pristanišču, na zidu pa je bil tudi njen brat. Kartice bodo v zapečatenih ovojnicah šle k njej; ona mu bo prebrala vsako številko in njegov odgovor primerjala s kartico. Če odgovora ne bo na kartici, bodo končali. Nikogar ne bodo prosili, naj pride, in nikogar ne bodo prosili, naj odpusti. Davi je to dvakrat povedala spečim in budnim ter zapisala na hrbtno stran prošnje.

scenes.title: Razumen človek
paragraphs: *Soba guvernerja Theska · drugi dan, 19:00*
Ruvane Thesk je bil pod odejo droben, njegove roke pa zelo čiste. Devetim pristaniščem je vladal trideset let in se že v prvem naučil, da obiskovalca najhitreje razorožiš tako, da si ga vesel.

**Thesk**  
Točna si. Tako sem slišal. Prosim, sedi. Čaja ti ne morem ponuditi. Dajejo mi nekaj slabšega.
Illuminara je sedla. Pogoje mu je povedala v štirih stavkih in nato utihnila, ker so bili štirje stavki vse, kar je imela.
Vzel si je čas. Ko je spregovoril, je uporabil sproščeni ton človeka, ki je vodil veliko sestankov in želi pomagati.

**Thesk**  
Potem naj predlog izboljšam. Knjigo dobi moja hči. Ona je njena dedinja. Lahko odloči, komu bo služila. Darilo očeta hčeri, pa nikomur ni treba stati v hodniku.

**Illuminara**  
Ne.

**Thesk**  
Nisi slišala mojih razlogov.

**Illuminara**  
Enega sem slišala. Njo naredi za stvar, ki jo podariš. Povej mi preostale.

**Thesk**  
V tisti knjigi so uradniki, ki danes sedijo v pristaniških uradih. Nekateri so zdaj spodobni. Nekateri imajo otroke, ki so se rodili pozneje. Izpraševalec v Sedmem pristanišču podpisuje dovoljenja vsakemu pilotu v Pristaniščih, pa je na štirideseti strani. Če njegovo ime prebereš polni sobi, preden ga je sodišče karkoli vprašalo, do petka noben pilot od njega ne bo sprejel dovoljenja in nihče ne bo letel. Predlagaš, da prižgano vžigalico vržeš v državo, ki je bila trideset let tiha. In za to ti bodo ploskali.
To je bil njegov najmočnejši argument, in vedel je, da je, Illuminara pa se ni pretvarjala, da je šibek.

**Illuminara**  
Za izpraševalca nisem vedela. Njegovega imena ne morem vzeti iz knjige, pa tudi ti ga ne moreš. Ali jo lahko preberemo tako, da bo Sedmo pristanišče v petek še vedno imelo izpraševalca?

**Thesk**  
Ne vem. O tem se sprašujem že od raketoplana.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bom to odnesla njim kot nekaj, kar si povedal. Ne kot pogoj. Lahko zavrnejo.

Zaprl je oči in za trenutek je bil videti svojih let. Ko jih je odprl, je knjigo potegnil čez odejo proti njej; črno platno je bilo na vogalih že osivelo. Odprl jo je in ji pokazal strani. S palcem je šel čez enainštirideset strani, ne da bi se jih dotaknil, kakor človek stopi čez stopnico, za katero ve, da je zlomljena.

**Thesk**  
Zadnjih enainštirideset vnosov ni v moji pisavi. Moj namestnik Corvin Hale jih je vodil v lastni stenografiji, mrtev pa je že devet let. Preberem lahko številke in imena. Ne morem prebrati, kje so. Knjiga z enainštiridesetimi stranmi, ki jih ne morem prebrati, ni knjiga, ki bi jo lahko pravilno izročil. Zaradi tega slabo spim.

Illuminara je opazovala, kako je palec znova šel čeznje, in razumela, kaj se je skrivalo pod prijaznostjo. Ni bil strah pred vžigalico, uradniki ali celo hčerjo. Bil je uradnikov strah pred nedokončano stranjo.

**Illuminara**  
Obrazec vsako družino prosi za dejstvo, ki ga pozna samo ona, in ga primerja s tvojo stranjo. Kjer je tvoja stran prazna, njihova morda ni.

**Thesk**  
Pomagali bi mi jo dokončati.

**Illuminara**  
Pomagali bi sebi. Ne bi pomagali tebi.

**Thesk**  
Da. Tako je treba povedati.
Dolgo je molčal.

**Thesk**  
In Ilen?

**Illuminara**  
Nič ni obljubljeno. Odločila se bo pozneje in lahko reče ne.

**Thesk**  
Torej naj izročim edino stvar, ki jo imam, in za nič.

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Thesk**  
Tega nisem storil še nikoli.

**Illuminara**  
Verjamem ti.

Roka mu je šla k kozarcu na pladnju in se tako močno tresla, da se je voda polila. Illuminara je prišla prva in mu ga pridržala. Ni vedela, ali je držati kozarec temu človeku prijaznost ali sostorilstvo, pa ga je vseeno držala, ker je bil pred njo, in zaradi tega ni ničesar trdila ne njemu ne sebi.

**Thesk**  
Zakaj si tukaj? Zaradi nje? Zaradi njih?

**Illuminara**  
Zaradi tistega, ki je pred menoj. Nocoj si to ti. Ne bom ti rekla, da je vse v redu.

**Thesk**  
Dobro. Sicer bi ti nehal verjeti.
Kozarec je sam odložil.

**Thesk**  
Pripelji svojo uradnico ob šestih.

scenes.title: Stran za stranjo
paragraphs: *Registrska soba, Vesper Rest · tretji dan, 06:00*

Registrska soba je bila edini prostor na asteroidu z dovolj veliko mizo, Hesper Duell pa jo je uredila tako, kakor je urejala sobe štirideset let: guvernerjev stol na enem koncu, miza z zapečatenimi ovojnicami na drugem, med njima pa nič razen knjige. Bila je večja, kot si jo je Illuminara predstavljala, in preprostejša, vezana v črno platno, na vogalih osivelo. Ob njej je stala odprta druga, manjša soba z dvema stoloma.
Illuminara je v zgodnjih urah Davij prinesla vprašanje izpraševalca. Pričakovala je zavrnitev, pa so ji rekli, naj počaka do jutra.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Zaradi njega ne bom dovolila zadržati niti enega imena. Niti enega.

**Hesper Duell**  
Nič ne bo zadržano. Vsako stran najprej v celoti preberemo v manjši sobi družini, ki ji pripada. Dvorana jo sliši, če tako želijo. Vsako stran, ki imenuje uradnika, še vedno na položaju, bom isto uro s svojo roko prepisala sodnemu registratorju. Sodišče ga lahko umakne z delovnega mesta. Soba, polna nas, ga ne more.

**Davi Orsolo**  
In petek? Sedmo nima izpraševalca.

**Hesper Duell**  
Sedmo nima izpraševalca, dokler sodišče ne konča. To je cena, plačajo pa jo piloti, ki niso storili ničesar.
Davi je za trenutek pogledala odprta vrata manjše sobe, nato knjigo.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Potem beri.
Trideset družin je napisalo kartice. Hesper je prvo ovojnico odprla z nožem za pisma.

**Hesper Duell**  
Stran štiriindevetdeset. Kaj je rekla pri vratih?

**Thesk**  
V vnosu piše: »Ali je čajnik pristavljen?« Pisana je z drobno roko. Spodaj je opomba: »Zasmejala se je.«
Hesper je pogledala kartico v svoji roki, nato guvernerja, in ni rekla nič. Ženska, ki jo je napisala, je stala v vratih, Illuminara pa je opazovala, kako ji je roka segla k ustom.
Ujemalo se jih je devetindvajset od tridesetih. Trideseta kartica je bila od družine, katere stran je bila zapisana v Halejevi stenografiji.

**Thesk**  
Te ne morem prebrati. Lahko bi si izmislil nekaj, kar bi vam bilo všeč. Raje bi, da veste, katero je kaj.

**Hesper Duell**  
Ponarejevalec vrzel zapolni. On jo je pustil. Nadaljuj.

Tako se je knjiga začela. Bral je po štirideset minut, nato mu je zmanjkalo glasu in so čakali, nihče pa mu ni rekel, naj pohiti. Vsaka stran je šla najprej k svoji družini v manjšo sobo, večina družin pa je nato prosila, naj jo znova prebere v dvorani; nekaj jih ni. Illuminara je sedela ob vratih z rokami na kolenih in počela to, kar je počelo okno, nič več: preprečevala je, da bi soba postala oder kogarkoli. Imen ni mogla narediti lažjih.
Pri dvesto dvanajsti strani se je ustavil in ni mogel nadaljevati.

**Thesk**  
Te ne morem.
Illuminara ni rekla nič. Tudi Hesper ne. Soba je čakala. Čez čas je stran potegnil k sebi in začel.
Stran Pella Orsola je prišla malo po drugi uri naslednjega jutra. Davi je prosila za dvorano. Od polnoči je stala zadaj.

**Thesk**  
Orsolo, Pell. Pristaniški pilot, Deveto pristanišče. Kamnolom balastnega ledu, odsek C, štirideset metrov pod nakladalno tirnico. Žigosano premeščen, po ukazu guvernerja.
Davi se ni premaknila.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Še enkrat.

**Thesk**  
Orsolo, Pell. Pristaniški pilot. Odsek C, pod nakladalno tirnico. Po mojem ukazu.
Davi je pokimala, kakor se pokima odčitku, ki se ujema s karto, in odšla. Illuminara ji ni sledila.

Do zore četrtega dne so prebrali tristo enainsedemdeset strani. Ženska blizu zadnjega dela sobe se je spomnila, da so Halejevi ljudje kamnolomsko baržo imenovali *Vrabec*, in s tem zaprla eno od enainštiridesetih strani. Moški se je spomnil datuma. Do poldneva so ljudje, ki so jim pripadale, zaprli devetnajst Halejevih strani. Dvaindvajset jih je ostalo odprtih in nihče v sobi se ni pretvarjal, da niso.

Ko so prebrali zadnjo stran, je Hesper knjigo prevzela v hrambo registra in jo zapečatila s svojo vrvico. Thesk je prosil, da bi jo imel ob postelji, in pod temi pogoji mu jo je posodila, zapečateno, s potrdilom, na katerem je to pisalo. Zdaj iz nje ni bilo mogoče izrezati nobene strani. Strani je bilo mogoče samo brati.

scenes.title: Vrata
paragraphs: *Hodnik pred guvernerjevo sobo · četrti dan, 21:40*

Hesperjina razsodba se je na jutro začetka branja razširila po hodniku: trideset kartic, devetindvajset ujemanj, ena poštena vrzel. Posadke z lopatami so z večernim transporterjem že odšle proti kamnolomu v Devetem pristanišču, knjige mrtvih pa so naposled začele postajati knjige najdenih.
Ilen je stala na hodniku z dlanmi skritimi v rokavih. Illuminara je čakala korak stran, ker so jo prosili, naj čaka tam.

**Ilen**  
Rekla sem, naj bo knjiga prva. Bila je prva. Zdaj moram ugotoviti, ali sploh hočem.

**Illuminara**  
Še vedno lahko rečeš ne. Tukaj nihče ničesar ne dolguje.

**Ilen**  
Vem. Samo zato lahko vstopim.

Vrata so se odprla medicinski sestri in Illuminara je videla v sobo, preden so se zaprla. Ni je pripravil. Odeja je ležala postrani, dobri stol je stal ob zidu, kjer ga je pustila sestra, na pladnju pa ni bilo čaja. Ni se dvignil, da bi kogarkoli sprejel.

Ilen je vstopila sama. Illuminara je za njo ohranila okno zaprto in ni storila ničesar drugega. Šestindvajset minut. Skozi vrata sta prihajala dva glasova, eden miren in drugi raskav, raskavi pa ni bil vedno njegov.
Ko je Ilen prišla ven, je bila videti hkrati starejša in lažja.

**Ilen**  
Vprašal me je, ali sem jedla.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj si rekla?

**Ilen**  
Da je to zelo dobro vprašanje in da nanj ne bom odgovorila. Potem sem mu povedala vse. Ni me usmerjal. Poslušal je. Ne bom ti povedala, kaj je rekel.

**Illuminara**  
Ni ti treba.

Ruvane Thesk je umrl ob deset čez štiri z zapečateno knjigo zaprto na mizi ob postelji, izposojeno od Hesper, v roki pa je držal potrdilo njene uradnice. Illuminara je bila v sobi. Prosil je za nekoga, medicinska sestra pa je ostala brez prostovoljcev. Ni ga prijela za roko in ni odšla. Ko je bilo konec, je sestri povedala čas.

scenes.title: Odsek C
paragraphs: *Kamnolom balastnega ledu, Deveto pristanišče · peti dan, 06:30*

Nakladalna tirnica je bila belo pomrznjena, štirideset metrov pod njo pa je prva posadka prebila pokrov odseka. Davi je stala na robu v dvakrat ovitem šalu in imela v plašču stran, čistopis v Hesperjini urejeni pisavi, ki je z guvernerjevimi besedami povedal, kje je njen mož.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Nisem mu odpustila.

**Illuminara**  
Nihče te ni prosil.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Dobro. Ne prosi me.

**Davi Orsolo**  
Sedmo pristanišče danes zjutraj nima izpraševalca. Polovica pilotov v Pristaniščih je prizemljena, dokler sodišče ne zasede, nekateri pa pravijo, da smo krivi mi.

**Illuminara**  
Smo. Hočeš, da rečem drugače?

**Davi Orsolo**  
Ne.

Spodaj v izkopu je lopata zazvenela ob led, nato ob nekaj, kar ni bilo led. Ob robu so ljudje, ki so štiri dni molče stali v hodniku, drug za drugim začeli govoriti. Davi je vzela stran in jo na glas prebrala svojemu sinu, ki je imel sedem let, ko se pilotni čoln ni vrnil. Prebrala jo je dvakrat, ker so ji povedali, da sme.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara odkrije, da so vijolični žigi oštevilčeni sklici in ne odgovori, sprejme Davijin nasprotni primer ter zoži svojo trditev, nato pa družinam odnese Theskov najmočnejši ugovor, ne da bi ga spremenila v njegov pogoj; družine, njihova uradnica, Ilen in celo Thesk ohranijo svoje odločitve, overjena knjiga pa vrne 390 lokacij, 22 jih pošteno pusti odprtih, uradnike na položajih usmeri proti sodišču ter Davi pripelje do kamnoloma Pella Orsola, ne da bi zahtevala odpuščanje.
